limitations_and_boundaries: The study is limited to the barrel cortex of mice; findings may not generalize to other brain regions or species.
The transient nature of the microglial recruitment deficit and synaptic maturation impairment suggests that compensatory mechanisms may exist.
The study does not directly test the mechanisms by which microglia influence glutamate receptor maturation (e.g., phagocytosis vs. soluble factors).

research_questions.statement: How does CX3CR1 deficiency affect microglial cell recruitment and functional maturation of thalamocortical synapses in the developing barrel cortex?

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: Impaired functional maturation of thalamocortical synapses in CX3CR1 deficient mice

provenance.text_excerpt: Overall, our results show that CX3CR1 deficiency induced a transient impairment in the maturation of glutamate receptor functional expression at thalamocortical synapses of layer 4 neurons.

claims.statement: CX3CR1 deficiency impairs the functional maturation of postsynaptic glutamate receptors at thalamocortical synapses, as evidenced by reduced AMPAR/NMDAR ratio and delayed GluN2B-to-GluN2A switch.

experiments_or_tasks: Whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings of layer 4 neurons in thalamocortical slices from CX3CR1+/eGFP, CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP, and CX3CR1+/+ mice at P5-P33 to measure AMPAR/NMDAR ratio, paired-pulse ratio, and NMDAR decay kinetics.

methods.name: Electrophysiology
methods.protocol_description: Thalamocortical slices (400 μm) from P5-P33 mice were prepared. Whole-cell recordings from layer 4 neurons with pipettes (3-5 MΩ) filled with CsMeSO3-based solution. EPSCs evoked by minimal stimulation of TCAs. AMPAR/NMDAR ratio measured at -70 mV and +40 mV. Paired-pulse ratio at 60 ms interval. NMDAR decay fitted with double exponential. Drugs: gabazine, D-AP5, NBQX, Ro256981. Statistical tests: Mann–Whitney U or unpaired t test.

results.value_raw_text: In CX3CR1+/eGFP mice, weighted decay time constant decreased from P5-P7 to P9-P10; in CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice, no significant change. At P9-P10, decay was significantly slower in CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP than CX3CR1+/eGFP. In adult (P27-P33), no difference between genotypes.

results.value_raw_text: Paired-pulse depression did not differ between CX3CR1+/eGFP and CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice over the developmental window (N ≥ 3 animals each).

provenance.text_excerpt: As expected, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio gradually increased in CX3CR1+/eGFP mice of P5 (N = 5, the number of cells n is given in Fig. 2G), P7 (N = 10) and P9 (N = 17; Fig. 2F). At this latter stage, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio of CX3CR1+/eGFP mice (0.75 ± 0.09) was not significantly different from that of CX3CR1+/+ mice (0.84 ± 0.12; n = 9, 3 animals). In contrast, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio at thalamocortical synapses of CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice did not change significantly over the same developmental window (Fig. 2F) with mean values remaining below 0.5 at P5 (N = 3), P7 (N = 5), and P9 (N = 6; Fig. 2G). Consequently, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio at P9 was significantly lower in CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP than in CX3CR1+/eGFP mice (Fig. 2G).

results.value_raw_text: In CX3CR1+/eGFP mice, AMPAR/NMDAR ratio increased from P5 to P9 (0.75 ± 0.09 at P9). In CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice, ratio remained below 0.5 at P5, P7, and P9; significantly lower than CX3CR1+/eGFP at P9.

results.value_raw_text: At P9-P10, Ro256981 (300 nM) reduced NMDAR charge more in CX3CR1+/eGFP than in CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice, indicating impaired GluN2B-to-GluN2A switch in CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP.

experiments_or_tasks: Immunohistochemistry and confocal imaging of tangential sections through layer 4 of barrel cortex in CX3CR1+/eGFP, CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP, and CX3CR1+/+ mice at P4-P9 and adult stages to quantify microglial cell distribution inside and outside TCA clusters.

methods.name: Immunohistochemistry
methods.protocol_description: Mice were perfused with 4% paraformaldehyde, brains fixed overnight, and 50-μm-thick tangential sections were immunostained for 5-HTT, VGluT2, Iba1, or CX3CL1. Secondary antibodies Alexa Fluor 546 or 633 and TO-PRO-3 were used. Confocal images were analyzed with ImageJ.

methods.name: Quantitative analysis of microglial distribution
methods.protocol_description: Number of microglial cells inside and outside TCA clusters (immunostained for 5-HTT or VGluT2) was counted in tangential sections through layer 4. Six barrels of rows B and C were considered per animal. Data presented as mean ± SEM; statistical evaluation with one-way ANOVA followed by Mann–Whitney U test.

study_units.name: Microglial cell distribution in barrel cortex

results.value_raw_text: No difference in overall microglial density in layer 4 of somatosensory cortex between CX3CR1+/eGFP and CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice at P7 (p=0.44).

provenance.text_excerpt: fractalkine immunoreactivity labels the barrels of the somatosensory cortex between P5 and P7 (Fig. 1G; N = 3). Before the formation of the barrels, at P3, fractalkine immunostaining was more diffuse and did not allow the identification of the barrels (N = 2) whereas in the adult cortex individual cells were immunostained in all cortical layers (N = 2; Fig. 1G).

results.value_raw_text: Fractalkine immunoreactivity labels barrels between P5 and P7; at P3 staining was diffuse; in adult, individual cells were immunostained in all cortical layers.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: Although MGCs were also distributed around TCA clusters at P5 (Fig. 1B), there was a significant deficit of MGCs inside TCA clusters of CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice at P6 and P7 (Fig. 1B,D). This deficit of MGC entry into the TCA clusters of CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice was transient and there was no difference in the I/O ratio between heterozygous and homozygous mice at P9 (Fig. 1D).

provenance.text_excerpt: The ratio of the number of microglia inside and outside TCA clusters (I/O ratio) increased progressively between P5 and P9 (Fig. 1D) and was closed to unity in the barrel field of adult mice (0.93 ± 0.10; N = 3; P60–P70). A similar developmental pattern was observed in CX3CR1+/+ mice with almost no microglia entering TCA clusters before P6 and an I/O ratio at P7 of 0.39 ± 0.19 (Fig. 1C; N = 3) similar to that observed in CX3CR1+/eGFP mice (Fig. 1D; p = 0.28).

results.value_raw_text: I/O ratio increased progressively between P5 and P9 in CX3CR1+/eGFP mice; at P7, I/O ratio in CX3CR1+/+ mice was 0.39 ± 0.19 (N=3), similar to CX3CR1+/eGFP (p=0.28). In CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice, I/O ratio was significantly lower at P6 and P7 compared to CX3CR1+/eGFP, but no difference at P9.
